messages:
sam (eng-security): alert: internal audit flagged a privilege-drift event - build-runner was granted broad iam roles during emergency ops last week. upstream runc fixes also landed. propose: coordinated base-image rebuild, KMS ephemeral signing, and a 48h audit backfill. we need owners and a short maintenance window.

rachel (eng-infra): ack. infra can schedule a 30m window tonight 02:30 UTC and freeze the builder pool for the cut. pipeline should tag staging+sha and write audit JSON to GCS. who will sign?

tony (eng-runtime): runtime ask: rebuild -> staging -> runtime fuzz (20m) + smoke -> 1% canary -> 10% -> full. add probes for prctl/ptrace and auto-rollback on kernel oops. ensure entrypoint drops CAP_SYS_ADMIN and set no_new_privs.

jaya (sec): i'll own KMS/audit correlation. prefer ephemeral unwrap (KMS wrapped key) for the pipeline rather than restoring long-lived signer perms. pipeline must emit structured events for build:start, image:push, image:sign, key:unwrap. example: {"actor":"svc:build-runner","event":"image:sign","image":"registry.stg/base:sha","signer":"kms://projects/redwood/keyRings/build/cryptoKeys/wrap","ts":"..."} - we can parse that, right?

rachel (eng-infra): yes. infra will write audit JSONL to gs://redwood-build-logs/rbld-30399-stg/audit.jsonl and grant read to security. cosign will use the KMS plugin: cosign sign --key ksm://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/build/cryptoKeys/wrap. we'll also deploy a quick-revoke endpoint to mark images untrusted.

ci-bot: CI: rebuild queued: id=rbld-30399-stg, initiator=sam. watch: https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/rbld-30399-stg

tony (eng-runtime): runtime checklist for the rebuilt base image:
- Dockerfile: ENV NO_NEW_PRIVS=1 and set no_new_privs metadata
- entrypoint: drop CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_MKNOD, CAP_SYS_MODULE
- containerd: default disable unprivileged userns remap for this image
- include sidecar for faster core collection and SBOM attestation

jaya (sec): audit backfill query i'm going to run (example):
logName="projects/redwood/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity"
protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:"build-runner@redwood"
(protoPayload.methodName:("SetIamPolicy" OR "roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator" OR "AsymmetricSign"))
timestamp>="2026-03-18T00:00:00Z" AND timestamp<"2026-03-20T00:00:00Z"
correlate matches with gs://redwood-build-logs/*/rbld-* and KMS audit entries for projects/redwood/keyRings/build.

sam (eng-security): add field "rbac_delta" to pipeline audit events when any manual IAM grants occur during the window. we'll filter on that to find surprises. if we detect any artifacts signed by the old/temporary principal in the window, we must mark them untrusted and run a rbld-resign flow.

ci-bot: CI: job rbld-30399-stg started: runner=builder-7 image=debian-14+runc-patch

rachel (eng-infra): infra notes:
- freeze builder pool at cut time for 7m
- tag registry as staging+sha and attach metadata: build-id, signer-kid, attest-token
- cosign sign as described and write structured audit to GCS
- quick-revoke endpoint POST /registry/v1/revoke {"image":"..."} available for emergencies

ci-bot: CI: job rbld-30399-stg completed: status=SUCCESS duration=11m artifacts at gs://redwood-build-logs/rbld-30399-stg/

jaya (sec): starting audit backfill now. will paste CSV to ticket when complete. please ensure sec-team has read ACL on the build logs (rachel).

rachel (eng-infra): granted security-team@redwood read to gs://redwood-build-logs/rbld-30399-stg/. audit JSONL is present at gs://redwood-build-logs/rbld-30399-stg/audit.jsonl

tony (eng-runtime): started staging canary. running runtime-fuzzer for 20m and eBPF probes for prctl/ptrace. auto-rollback on >1 kernel oops in 5m.

jaya (sec): audit correlation results: one sign event within the backfill window appears to be performed by build-runner@redwood at 2026-03-19T03:11:22Z and correlates to registry.stg/base:sha-abc123. marking that artifact as potentially untrusted and flagging for re-sign. attaching CSV to ticket.

sam (eng-security): owners: rachel=infra & registry revoke/resign, tony=runtime tests & canary fallback, jaya=KMS + audit correlation, sam=sec coord + incident runbook. infra: please POST revoke for registry.stg/base:sha-abc123 and run rbld-resign immediately.

rachel (eng-infra): executing POST /registry/v1/revoke {"image":"registry.stg/base:sha-abc123"}. kicking rbld-resign job: id=rbld-resign-30399 -> reads artifacts from gs://redwood-build-logs/rbld-30399-stg/artifacts/, re-signs with ephemeral KMS unwrap, and updates registry. will publish logs.

ci-bot: CI: rbld-resign-30399 started: runner=signer-1

tony (eng-runtime): canary shows no kernel oops so far, probes normal. fallback policy ready: if ptrace/prctl anomalies > threshold, route 100% of new traffic to runc-legacy pool and pause rollout.

ci-bot: CI: rbld-resign-30399 completed: status=SUCCESS duration=3m artifacts updated and new signature applied. registry revoke cleared after verification. logs: gs://redwood-build-logs/rbld-resign-30399/resign-log.txt

jaya (sec): audit follow-up: CSV and resign logs uploaded. no other unexpected sign/unwarp events found in window. adding runbook rule: disallow granting broad serviceAccount roles to build-runner without pre-approved ephemeral keyflow.

sam (eng-security): updating incident-runbook with exact queries, the rbld-resign flow, and quick-revoke endpoint. closing this coordination thread; will keep the runbook link here: https://wiki.redwood/internal/runbooks/privilege-drift-rebuild-2026. thanks all. :lock:
